The palps of the female, beside the proboscis:
As long as the proboscis; at rest the body is at an angle to the surface
Much shorter than the proboscis; at rest the body is parallel to the surface
The tip of the abdomen of the female:
Pointed, the cerci sticking out; legs often banded in white
Blunt, rounded
The white scales on the back of the thorax (the scutum):
In the shape of a lyre
One stripe down the middle
The bristles in front of the spiracle of the thorax (spiracular setae):
Present
Absent
Anopheles
The genus of the mosquitoes that carry malaria.
Aedes aegypti
The yellow fever mosquito, which also carries dengue, Zika and chikungunya.
Aedes albopictus
The Asian tiger mosquito, which can carry dengue and chikungunya too.
Culex
The common house mosquitoes, which carry the West Nile virus.
Culiseta
Large mosquitoes, most of which bite birds and other animals more than people.
